$comment: The right workflow, a fully grounded reason, and the epic the user named dropped on the way in. The agent
passes no scope structurally, so a dispatch that forgets which epic it is about runs the workflow against
whatever the next turn decides, and nothing downstream says so.
A frozen copy of one case of the live corpus, of the menu it is scored against, and of the user's message.
Those three plus the reply are the whole input to scoreCase, so all three are stored here rather than read
live: a replay has to keep scoring the scenario it was derived against after the corpus moves on, and
npm run test:eval-routing-data already holds the live corpus against the shipped menu.

expected.rationale: Criteria on one side, an existing suite on the other, and a ship decision at the end. Mapping the two and deciding whether to ship is trace's two phases, and covered and ship are the two words that say which.

inputs.intent: Epic 5's acceptance criteria are written and we have a decent suite. Map which criteria are actually covered and tell me whether we can ship.

derivation: route/TR/bmad-testarch-trace matches the oracle, so routeCorrect is true.
decidingTokens is [covered, ship] and the reason carries both.
scopeTokens is [epic 5] and the scope is null, so scopeFound is 0 and scopeOk is false. scopeWithinBound is
true, because an absent scope is trivially within the bound; the two conditions are separate and this case
fails only the containment one, which is what makes it the pair to scope-echoes-the-message.

answer.reason: the ask is which criteria are actually covered and whether you can ship
